title: Give the player a choice
blurb: The president asks a question with buttons and answers differently for each one.
how: choose([...]) shows one button for each thing in the list. prompt is the question above them.
It gives back a number: 0 if the player picked the first button, 1 for the second, and so on. Counting starts at 0.
pick = yield choose(...) saves that number in pick. Then if pick == 0: runs the lines under it only for the first button, and else: runs for anything else.
The lines under if and else are pushed in by four spaces. That's how Python knows which lines belong to which answer.
